title: Name the flag an unsupported-shape refusal actually refused
action: At the unsupported_argument_shape branch in router.rs (the final fallback after the missing-required check), diff the attempted argv's --flags against the resolved entry's schema properties. When one or more flags are unknown, name every one of them in the message, and for each offer the nearest declared spelling when the edit distance is small enough to be worth printing (reuse the crate's existing nearest-match helper if one exists — the unknown-command path already suggests spellings; do not write a second implementation). When NO flag is unknown — an out-of-enum value, a target that does not exist — keep today's wording, which is accurate in exactly that case. Honors cli-ergonomics D1 (8ef2bae6): every problem named in one message. Tests: an unknown flag is named with its suggestion (the live case was `state route --lane-value` against the declared --lane); two unknown flags are BOTH named; a call whose flags are all declared keeps today's exact bytes.

truths: An unknown flag is named in the refusal, with a nearest-spelling suggestion when one is close
Every unknown flag is named, not just the first
A refusal with no unknown flag keeps today's exact wording
The full declared test suite is green

trace.outcome: unsupported_argument_shape now names every unknown flag with a nearest-spelling suggestion; unchanged when all flags are declared
